newsitem.title: FRANCE: Lot to boost ex-Paris cargo capacity.
newsitem.headline: Lot to boost ex-Paris cargo capacity.

text.p: Poland's state-owned national carrier LOT said planned increases in its Paris-Charles de Gaulle to Warsaw passenger service will also boost cargo capacity on the route.

"At present, we operate a daily flight with a Boeing 737-400 offering up to three tonnes of freight. From the start of April, we are going to progressively introduce additional flights and by June we could be operating two daily frequencies between Paris and Warsaw," a CDG-based LOT cargo official told Reuters.

"While the decision to add flights is passenger led, we have been steadily building up cargo volumes since opening a CDG sales office in January 1996. The new, daily frequency is scheduled to leave Paris at around 0700(local time), so there could be a niche market for express shipments," the official said.
On LOT's Paris-Warsaw service shipments are largely made up of pharmaceuticals, cosmetics and spare parts, hel added.
LOT also operates scheduled 737 passenger services from Paris to Krakow and from Lyon and Nice to Krakow.

Unlike freight, LOT's passenger services from France are code-shared with Air France. However, this agreement will cease from March 31, 1997 and LOT will operate independently of the French national carrier, the official said. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+5017
